A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ET-SAM. All 20 pages of v1 and 21 pages of v2, including their appendices, are readable; figures, tables, equations, and relocated content support reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendices A–B report original detection, layout-analysis, runtime, ablation, and controlled baseline results.

after.justification: The original empirical results remain, supplemented by loss-weight experiments, threshold-dependent timing, failure examples, and comparative latency measurements.

M1.justification: The point decoder, task prompts, hierarchical mask decoder, joint training, pseudo-labeling, and inference procedures remain unchanged. Equation 2 already used heatmap loss weight 50 in v1; v2 tests alternative weights without changing the adopted method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same six training datasets and the same quantitative evaluation coverage on HierText, Total-Text, CTW1500, and ICDAR2015. TextSeg qualitative examples are retained within the reorganized Figure 6. The new analyses introduce no distinct dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: The existing accuracy-comparison sets remain unchanged. New Appendix C/Table 11 evaluates DPText-DETR, labeled DPText, and SRFormer as latency comparators; their earlier participation was in accuracy comparisons.

E3.justification: V2 adds evaluation configurations using heatmap loss weights 25, 50, and 100, plus A800 timing across point thresholds and a HierText comparison of encoding and decoding latency. Existing splits, metrics, training schedules, and default settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 adds loss-weight sensitivity testing, extends the existing point-threshold analysis to latency, and introduces comparative efficiency analysis and explicit failure examples. These provide additional diagnostics; the center-point heatmap analysis and controlled DPText-DETR comparison already appeared in v1's appendices.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run variability, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The added results retain point-estimate and average reporting without introducing uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in the eight matched original tables are unchanged, including v1 Tables 7–8 becoming v2 Tables 9–10. New Tables 7, 8, and 11 add timing and loss-weight results; for example, Table 11 reports encoding latency of 0.291s for ET-SAM versus 0.015s for each comparator. Figure 7 adds qualitative failures.

T1.justification: The heatmap definitions, tensor formulations, and loss equations remain unchanged, including the anisotropic Gaussian construction in Appendix A. No formal assumptions, theorems, proofs, or derivations are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: efficient point prompting, training with heterogeneous annotations, roughly 3× acceleration over Hi-SAM, and an average 11.0% F-score improvement on the three single-level benchmarks.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretations of the loss-weight tradeoff and latency bottlenecks, discusses background-related word-mask failures, and explicitly limits direct use for high-level multimodal understanding because vision-language alignment is absent. The curved-text limitation and training-data explanation for accuracy differences were already present.

D1.justification: V2 newly states that code and models are available through a repository link and specifies hardware for the timing analyses. Conversely, Section 4.2 removes explicit augmentation and resizing instructions, including the scaling range, in favor of referring to Hi-SAM. This changes documentation without establishing changed preprocessing.

R1.justification: Section 3.1 newly attributes the point-decoder paradigm to PseCo. V2 also adds citations to I3CL, GoMatching, GoMatching++, TextFuseNet, and DeepSolo++, removes the copy-paste augmentation reference, and emphasizes compatibility with other SAM-based methods.

P1.justification: V2 streamlines several passages, corrects grammar, standardizes some ICDAR2015 terminology, and revises author and header information. It expands the conclusion to include limitations and adds acknowledgements and Appendix C, while retaining the main narrative and section order.

P2.justification: Figure 6 merges the earlier single-level examples with two retained HierText examples, dropping the third HierText example. Figure 7 becomes a failure-case display. Three tables are added, and existing appendix tables are relocated and renumbered; the architecture figures and established table designs remain largely unchanged.

improvement.justification: The added sensitivity tests, comparative latency measurements, failure examples, and explicit limitations modestly strengthen experimental support and clarify applicability. PseCo attribution and the reported code/model link improve transparency. These benefits are partly offset by removing explicit preprocessing instructions; the revision provides a limited net improvement while retaining the original method and benchmark results.
